exclude_reasons.planet_atmospheres_avg_mol_wgt: derived from the gas fractions (audit check 1): LOO R2 1.0 via linear, all gases; max single-gas |r| 0.914; permutation null 99.9th pct 0.226
exclude_reasons.planet_density: redundant with planet_radius_in_km (r=0.969, LOO R² 0.94) — kept radius as the more direct measurement, dropped to avoid a wasted degree of freedom on 30 rows.
exclude_reasons.PlanetIndex: row identifier, not a physical property — excluded to prevent the model memorizing individual rows rather than learning from features, especially critical at only 30 rows.

leakage_audit.method: LOO R2 of OLS fits: all gases, best 1-3 gas subsets, best 1-4 non-gas column subsets (linear and log-log); exact binning of low-cardinality columns; T_eq formula. Flag if LOO R2 >= 0.98 or |r| >= 0.98 and above the 99.9th pct of a 500-permutation null.

near_misses_for_review.fit: non-overlapping bins of star_temperature_in_Kelvin, permutation p = 0.004 (levels too small to confirm): {'3': [5909.6192, 5909.6192, 1], '4': [5312.0731, 5890.5555, 27], '5': [5284.2351, 5298.0471, 2]}

leakage_audit.note: JSON has no comments, so each exclusion's reasoning is in exclude_reasons.

decisions.planet_density: excluded (see exclude_reasons); planet_radius_in_km retained as a feature
decisions.star_class: star_class retained as a feature — binning pattern plausible (non-overlapping temperature ranges) but not statistically confirmed due to sparse classes (3 and 5 have 1-2 rows). Re-run audit_inara_leakage.py's binning check once INARA has more rows per class.
